Looking at this from the farmer's perspective in Quzhou County, Hebei:

---

My family has farmed this land for generations. I know one system: winter wheat, then summer corn on the same fields, back and forth every year. That's what the land here is for. That's what everyone does. I have about 10 mu — enough for me to manage alone, since my son moved to the city.

For wheat, I plant in October like always. I buy the improved seed from the seed shop in town — same kind most of my neighbors use, reliable. I put down compound fertilizer and urea as base before I plow it under with the rotary machine. I water it before it gets cold, water it again in spring when it wakes up, water at jointing, and once more when the grain is filling. Four waterings. I spray once for aphids in spring — they always come. Maybe once more if I see leaf disease. Harvest in June.

The same day or next day after wheat harvest, I plant corn. Everyone uses hybrid seed now. I tried traditional seed years ago — it doesn't compare. For corn, I don't plow — I seed directly into the stubble. Saves my back and time. Corn gets more nitrogen — I split it: some at planting, some when it's knee-high. I water once if summer stays dry, but usually the rains help. I check for corn borer and spray if I see damage.

I don't change much year to year. What worked last year works this year.
